statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 55 in the elevated band on an unrestarted Saudi East-West pipeline, WTI marked $100.05, Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandeb approach and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 90 percent for an increase. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour, including a new Saturday de-escalation step in Baghdad.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, twelve hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. Third, the only new verified development this hour is de-escalatory: Iraq dismissed its Maysan Operations Command commander and opened an investigative council after confirming the drones originated from its territory, while Riyadh continues to withhold retaliation. No evidence-based danger window is published, because no window inside this horizon contains a tradeable session. Stress at 55 describes an unresolved Gulf supply picture and a hawkishly priced policy week; under the fixed mapping Stress does not alter the machine state on its own.
headline: Almost fifteen hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI $100.05, and the weekend's first verified development leans further toward de-escalation: Iraq dismissed the commander of its Maysan Operations Command early Saturday after confirming the drones that shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline came from Iraqi territory.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found the price picture unchanged. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having closed near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation still shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95%, a curve consistent with a hawkish policy path rather than a growth scare.

The macro backdrop is hawkish and already priced. Friday's core CPI rose 0.3% on the month against a 0.2% consensus, with core at 2.4% on the year, headline CPI at 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, and market pricing for a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September decision now cited near 90 percent. That meeting also carries updated economic projections and a press conference thirty minutes later, and the inherited calibration treats a multi-stage policy sequence as a case for care rather than an automatic Tail block. Those are Wednesday checkpoints that sit well outside this horizon.

The Gulf picture is the main open question, and it moved slightly toward de-escalation overnight. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which normally carries roughly 5 million barrels per day toward Yanbu on the Red Sea and bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, remains shut as a precaution after drone strikes near Riyadh and Medina, with no announced restart date. Riyadh condemned the attack but said it would not respond at this stage following a request from Baghdad. Iraq then confirmed the drones originated from its territory, dismissed the commander of the Maysan Operations Command early on Saturday and ordered an investigative council. Separately, GCC, Iraqi and Iranian foreign ministers are due to meet in Salalah, Oman on Monday to discuss shipping and security in the strait. WTI is marked $100.05 after a 2.37% Friday decline and Brent $104.61, the pullback attributed to those talks.

None of this changes the mechanical read for this horizon. Every one of the twenty-four forecast slots lies inside the CME weekend closure, so the shallow pullbacks, failed retracements and session-extreme holding that define Tail cannot be observed or formed. Conditional Tail therefore drifts from 6 to a 10 cap purely as a function of accumulating unpriced headline exposure, and every slot maps to EA_ON and green. Stress runs 55 to 58 and carries the environment: an offline bypass line, oil above $100, a constrained Hormuz route and a policy decision with projections. Confidence decays from 85 to 80 but stays inside the high band, because the binding limitation this weekend is the freshness of price rather than any gap in coverage. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was checked and was outside its freshness and completeness gate this hour, so it was not relied upon; the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 11:00 UTC on 11 September to 10:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens in a trend-up read with Tail at 14 as the European advance extended. The 12:30 UTC inflation print produced the only elevated readings of the window, Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and then 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, then fell to 13 and 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final thirteen slots sit at Tail 5 and 6 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 82 to 56 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, twelve hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps to 7, 8 and 9 at four-hour intervals before capping at 10 for the final eight slots as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs 55 to a 58 ceiling and describes the environment rather than a path: a Saudi East-West pipeline outage with no restart date, WTI marked $100.05 after a 2.37% Friday decline, Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandeb approach, and a 16 September policy decision with projections priced near 90 percent for an increase. Confidence decays from 85 to 80, remaining inside the high band because the evidence set is complete and primary-sourced; the limitation is the freshness of price, not the coverage. The named checkpoints outside this horizon are the Monday foreign ministers' meeting in Salalah, the Sunday evening futures reopen and Wednesday's policy decision.
